precepts.text: This is talking about ancient Egypt. Bring it up to today: the enchantments today is called science, Esau's science, his technology. Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God. As it was then, it's going to be now. That's when they're going to acknowledge we're the sons of God: when death come, great death.
precepts.point: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour: that's Jacob. And another unto dishonour: that's Esau.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” Paul is comparing Esau to Pharaoh. Pharaoh was the world's superpower. In the time of Paul and the apostles, Rome was the Pharaoh of the time; Paul says Esau because Rome read every letter at its checkpoints and nobody could speak ill against Rome. The Lord did not smite Rome; Rome just transformed. Now we are in America, the world superpower, with more bombs and greater technology than any nation, 850 bases covering the planet. Nobody can defeat them one on one; God has to take them down.

Wisdom shows how it ended in Egypt: “For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” Bring it up to today: the enchantments today are called science, Esau's science, his technology. They will not believe anything because of it.

As it was then, it is going to be now. When death comes, great death, that is when they are going to acknowledge we are the sons of God. When this country is destroyed, the same thing that happened in the time of Moses will happen: everybody is going to say, we heard what your God did for you.

“and whom he will he hardeneth”. He hardened Pharaoh, and he is going to harden Esau. So do not believe the ones teaching that the white man will let millions of Israelites take his planes and boats to the wilderness; that is not in the Bible. The Israelites are as the sand of the sea, and no nation on this earth is going to let all of us come there.

precepts.text: So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous and destruction of the enemies. There can be no salvation of the oppressed without the destruction of the oppressor. That is so plain, but for Christians it's so difficult to understand.
precepts.point: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, give up; and to the south, keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee”, and “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” When it says give men for thee, it means kill men for thee. We don’t have to do anything; God says, let me do it. Wisdom of Solomon shows why it must be that way: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies go together. There can be no salvation without the destruction of your enemies. There can be no salvation of the oppressed without the destruction of the oppressor. That is so plain, but for Christians it is so difficult to understand.

That is what happened in Egypt, and it is what Isaiah promises again. Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba were given for Israel’s ransom because Israel was “precious in my sight”, “honourable”, and loved of God. The nations fall in Israel’s place.

And with the destruction comes the gathering: “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” The same judgment that destroys the oppressor sets the righteous free and brings every one that is called by his name home.

precepts.text: When the noblest offspring of the Egyptians was destroyed in one moment, they who would believe nothing by reason of the enchantments acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.
precepts.point: It is in our DNA: anything we do we excel at, while being held back; that is why reading was a crime for a slave and why every revolt began with slaves who read.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
In 1 Samuel 4 the Philistines heard the great shout “in the camp of the Hebrews”, and that is us. The ark of the covenant had come into our possession, and we rejoiced. They said, “Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.” The Philistines called us gods, mighty Gods. Wisdom of Solomon 18 shows the Egyptians coming to the same place.

“So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed.” That is when Christ came down and killed all the firstborn of the Egyptians, all the Egyptians’ babies.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments.” The Egyptians did not believe anything we had to say about being God’s people, by reason of their witches. “Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” After God gave them hell, they realized: these are the sons of God, these are God’s children.

The heathen have always known it. Don’t think for one second these Asians don’t understand it today; that is why they dumb us down on purpose. It is in our DNA: anything we do we excel at, while being held back at the same time. Why do you think it was a law for us not to read, and they would kill those that did know how to read? Because every time we read we start learning who we are, and then we start rising up. Many slave revolts took place where the slaves started reading and rose up and killed their masters, and they hid all of it. We are on another level in our DNA, and the nations acknowledge us to be the sons of God.

precepts.text: For in the long garment was the whole world: the high priest's ephod carried a stone for each tribe. The world on Aaron's chest was Israel, and Christ is the new high priest.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Remember, Christ is the new high priest. Wisdom shows what the high priest carried: “For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and thy Majesty upon the diadem of his head.”

That is Aaron the high priest, and the long garment is the ephod. There was a stone for each tribe. The whole world on Aaron’s chest was Israel. It did not represent the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Hittites, the Perizzites or the Ishmaelites; only the Israelites.

That is how 1 John 2:2 is understood: Christ is “the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” The world the high priest bore before God on the day of atonement was the twelve tribes, and the world Christ atones for as the new high priest is scattered Israel.

precepts.text: Solomon gave the same account Moses gave. While all things were in quiet silence, thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war. The word of God, the anointed Christ, has a throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he came down for war; he leaped off his throne. That is why Moses says the Lord God is a man of war. He brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death. A lot of you did not fully understand what Passover is really about: it is about death and destruction of the enemies of Israel. And the Lord sent the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams, so they should not perish without knowing why they were afflicted.
precepts.point: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea. Who did that? The Lord. Thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy. This is the wars of the Lord we are reading about: when the Lord fought against the Egyptians, drowned them in the Red Sea, and brought plagues upon them.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Some people still question it and say the Lord in Exodus 15:3 is the Father. Solomon gave the same account Moses gave. “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”.

Who is the word of God? The anointed, Christ. He has a royal throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he leaped off his throne and came down for war. So when Moses says “The Lord is a man of war”, he is speaking of the word of God that came down at the Passover, killed the Egyptians and drowned them in the Red Sea. Moses said it because he saw the Lord warring for his people.

He “brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” The Lord filled all things with death when he came down in Exodus. A lot of you do not fully understand what Passover is really about: it is about death and destruction of our enemies.

“Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.” The Lord sent the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams; he was afflicting them and warring with them. That is the right hand of Exodus 15:6 that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy.”

precepts.text: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people: his people are the Israelites; that is possessive. As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets: that we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform the mercy promised to our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to remember his holy covenant. That we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear: because in ancient Egypt we were fearful to serve our God, the same way some of you today are scared to even ask for a day off. Christ is going to return and redeem us from the hands of our enemies. That is Passover: deliverance.
precepts.point: Some of you are trying to save your enemy. Imagine back in Egypt, the Lord sends Moses to deliver the children of Israel, and the Israelites are fighting to save the Egyptians. That does not make sense, and it is what is happening today. The problem is many of our people do not even know who their enemy is: the enemy is the powers that enslaved and oppress you, and scripture says all the nations that touched Israel are going to answer for it.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Wisdom says “of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” There can be no salvation without your enemy being destroyed. Luke shows that this is what salvation always meant.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”. His people: that is possessive, and his people are the Israelites. “And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. Saved from who? Our enemies.

Who is your enemy, black man, black woman? Some are scared to say it for fear of losing their job. Yes, Satan is your enemy, but he works with his children, and his children are the Caucasian race. Not just the white man: the Arabs and all nations are going to pay for what they did to our people. Teach your kids that these people do not love you; from the mother’s womb we have been fighting with them. We live in a false illusion that everybody is equal and everybody loves everybody. Our enemies enslaved us, destroyed us, scattered us in slavery and took our land, and all nations hate us.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”: the mercy promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the covenant he made with us. “That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. That is Passover right there. Today we are in the hands of our enemies, and Christ is going to return and redeem us from them. And for that to happen, they all got to die, the same way the Lord drowned all the Egyptians in the sea.

“Might serve him without fear”, because in ancient Egypt we were fearful to serve our God. When we asked to go sacrifice, Pharaoh said we had too much idle time and gave us more work. It is the same today when you ask for a day off and are afraid you will be fired. Deliverance means serving him “In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.”

So salvation is not your enemies getting saved. Imagine Moses coming to deliver Israel and the Israelites fighting to save the Egyptians; that is what is happening today. Passover is the wars of the Lord: the Lord making war on Egypt, destroying them, and saving his people.

precepts.text: For in all things, O Lord, thou didst magnify thy people, and glorify them, neither didst thou lightly regard them: but didst assist them in every time and place. Wherever we were, the Lord was always there fighting for us. Even in these last days, the Lord will help us.
precepts.point: Some of you are trying to save your enemy. Imagine back in Egypt, the Lord sends Moses to deliver the children of Israel, and the Israelites are fighting to save the Egyptians. That does not make sense, and it is what is happening today. The problem is many of our people do not even know who their enemy is: the enemy is the powers that enslaved and oppress you, and scripture says all the nations that touched Israel are going to answer for it.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Wisdom closes the account of the Lord’s wars on Egypt the way chapter 18 described them: salvation for his people and destruction for their enemies. “For in all things, O Lord, thou didst magnify thy people, and glorify them”. In all things the Lord magnified his people, the twelve tribes of Israel.

“Neither didst thou lightly regard them: but didst assist them in every time and place.” God assisted us in every time and wherever we were. The Lord was always there fighting for us, and even in these last days the Lord will help us.

That is why the class went on to Jehoshaphat: “Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” Don’t be scared of armies and people. Teach and speak the word of God no matter what they threaten you with, because the Lord is always there fighting with you.

When an army surrounded Elisha, his servant cried, “Alas, my master! how shall we do?” Elisha answered, “Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” The Lord opened the young man’s eyes, “and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” Angels just waiting for the word. The same thing will come in the future: agents will surround houses and come for some of you. You cannot see it spiritually, but the Lord and his angels are with us, and the growth of IUIC and of Israel could only be accomplished because the Lord is with us, assisting his people in every time and place.

precepts.text: Of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies: do not be scared when your enemies' blood is shed, even if some splatters on you.
precepts.point: It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him; as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life. That is the difference between the twelve tribes and the heathen, the fake Jews and the Iranians alike.

note.label: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.why:
The brother about to die said, “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” It is good that this mortal body is slain when you look for a resurrection from the Almighty. “As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life”: as for the heathen, the fake Jews, the Iranians, the other nations, there is no resurrection for them. There is a difference between the twelve tribes of Israel and the other nations. The Most High made a covenant with our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Wisdom of Solomon goes along with it, and this has to be your mindset concerning salvation and gathering with your people: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of those who are against you come together.

So don’t get scared, y’all. Don’t be scared when you see your enemies’ blood being shed. Maybe some blood might splatter on you. Don’t get scared. The Lord has got our back, and we will not fear what man can do to us: you can kill this body, and we look to be raised again.

Until we receive our homeland, we are all we got. We are pilgrims here, with no favorite place, only our favorite people, the faithful brothers and sisters who keep the commandments. So we must keep the unity, show ourselves friendly, exhort each other, and show charity and mercy one to another.

precepts.text: Wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” Do you think the nations are just going to give his people back? No. Christ comes with armies: “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” Wherever the Israelites are, the armies of God will go there and deliver us and destroy those nations.

The Christian mentality wants a white Jesus to come back throwing flowers, and John Hagee says Christ will set his government up to get the Democrats and Republicans in order. Wisdom of Solomon shows what salvation really is: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” We all want the salvation of the righteous, and we have to accept the destruction of the enemy too. That is what we just read in Isaiah 43.

“For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The same way he punishes our adversaries, he glorifies us. That is the bride of Christ: Christ is coming to get his woman. That is what the whole thing is about.

So the redeeming of Isaiah 43:1, “I have called thee by thy name”, is the calling of Wisdom 18: “us, whom thou hadst called”, glorified by the very judgment that punishes the nations holding us.

precepts.text: The almighty word leaped down from heaven as a fierce man of war; the destroyer in Egypt was the word of God.
precepts.point: The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

precepts.why:
“the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.” Who was the destroyer? The Wisdom of Solomon tells it.

“For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction, And brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war, and standing up filled all things with death. The destroyer was the word of God.

And the destruction was total. “there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad for children that were bewailed. The master and the servant were punished after one manner; and like as the king, so suffered the common person. So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them”. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” The enchantments had kept them from believing; the death of the firstborn made them acknowledge Israel to be the sons of God. That is why none of Israel was to go out at the door until the morning: the word of God was in the land of destruction that night, and the Lord passed over the door where he saw the blood and would not suffer the destroyer to come in.

precepts.text: The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies were accepted together; the Lord glorified Israel by punishing the adversary.
precepts.point: Even the ground testified: where water stood before, dry land appeared, and a green field came up out of the violent stream; grass sprang up at the bottom of the sea for the people to pass.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
“Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.” Their salvation was Egypt's destruction, in the same hour: the Red Sea opened for Israel and closed on Egypt. We have to accept that.

The Wisdom of Solomon says it plainly. “Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing unto what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer. So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies were accepted together; the very thing that punished the adversary is what glorified Israel.

Whoever hates that the Most High saves one nation by destroying the others will have to come to grips with it. The people saw that great work, and “feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses.” The Lord who brought us out the first time with great signs and wonders will save Israel out of this captivity the same way, and that is why the brothers and sisters must have faith in these last days: a trial is the true test of faith.

precepts.text: In the long garment was the whole world; the four rows of stones bearing the twelve tribes are called the whole world and the glory of the fathers.
precepts.point: That settles 1 John 2:2 for the Christians who run to it. John was a Jew of the southern kingdom, so our sins means the southern kingdom; and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world means all twelve tribes, the whole world of Israel. Alongside Isaiah 45:17 and John 18:20, Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 is the precept that shows who the whole world is.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
The breastplate of judgment is set with “four rows of stones”, and “the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.” As with the shoulder stones, the nation is written on the priest.

The Wisdom of Solomon says of this very garment: “For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven”. The four rows of stones bearing the twelve tribes are called the whole world, and the glory of the fathers is written in their stones.

There was no Moabite stone, no Jebusite stone and no Edomite stone in that breastplate. The whole world in the garment is the twelve tribes of Israel. Alongside Isaiah 45:17 and John 18:20, this is the scripture that shows who the whole world is.

precepts.text: Of the Most High's people is accepted both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies; the two always go together.
precepts.point: Israel's salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

precepts.why:
The house fell upon the lords and upon all the people that were therein, “So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.” Remember Judges 14:4: the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson’s failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god.

“So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The two always go together. Israel’s salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor, as he brought it on the Philistines through Samson.

precepts.text: This great deliverance is the good news, for a remnant of Israel is fighting for our enemies and against the remnant of Jacob, but the righteous will be accepted.
precepts.point: Great deliverance he gives to his king and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Great deliverance giveth he to his king”. This great deliverance is the good news: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

A remnant of Israel is fighting for our enemies and against the remnant of Jacob, but the righteous will be accepted. The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies go together, and that is why David gives thanks among the heathen and sings praises to his name.

precepts.text: He is coming back with vengeance to defend us.
precepts.point: The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee; send thee help from the sanctuary and strengthen thee out of Zion. When the time comes Christ is jumping down from heaven like he did in Egypt; we have to visualize this because it is a prophecy that will come true.

note.label: Psalm 20: The Lord Defends His Anointed

precepts.why:
“Send thee help from the sanctuary, and strengthen thee out of Zion”. Here is what that help looked like in Egypt: “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”.

“And brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” The Almighty word leaped down as a fierce man of war and filled all things with death.

When the time comes, Christ is jumping down from heaven like he did in Egypt. He is coming back with vengeance to defend us. We have to visualize this, because it is a prophecy that will come true: the name of the God of Jacob defending us in the day of trouble.

precepts.text: You have to accept the salvation of the righteous, those keeping God's commandments, and the destruction of the enemy; if you do not, Christianity, religion, and "God loves everybody" is still in your mind.
precepts.point: Sing unto the Lord, bless His name, show forth His salvation from day to day. Why show forth His salvation from day to day? Because salvation is only for the Israelites, but your mind has to be correct, your mind has to be in the right place.

note.label: Psalm 96: Declare His Glory Among the Heathen

precepts.why:
To show forth his salvation from day to day, your mind has to be in the right place about what that salvation is. “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” Both parts were accepted by his people, the salvation and the destruction together.

Salvation is only for the Israelites, and the righteous are those keeping God's commandments. You have to accept the salvation of the righteous, and you have to accept the destruction of the enemy. If you cannot accept the second part, then Christianity, religion and God loves everybody is still in your mind, and your mind is not yet correct to show forth his salvation.

precepts.text: A child of God is to accept both parts, the saving of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies.
precepts.point: This is our salvation and redemption. Every nation has held Israel captive at one time, not just the friendly neighborhood white man: the Assyrians, Babylon, Persia and the Medes, Greece and Rome, the many captivities in the book of Judges, the Arabs and Ishmael in the trans-Saharan slave trade, and America. Whosoever leads into captivity shall go into captivity.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

precepts.why:
“So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” A child of God is to accept both parts: the saving of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies. They come together.

That is why the word to Ammon reads the way it does. Both Moab and Ammon go into captivity, and both are promised a return, but the reckoning comes first. Afterward the Most High will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon; the destruction of the enemies is what makes the salvation. This is our salvation and redemption.

precepts.text: Passover was the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies.
precepts.point: The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
What the passover celebrates: “Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing unto what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer. So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

Passover is the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies, the celebration of Israel's deliverance. It makes no sense that Christ would have the very Greeks who had just enslaved Israel keep a feast that commemorates their own destruction. The Greeks at the feast were Israelites.

moments.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: I want you to meditate on this scripture, especially today, a special day the so-called white man is celebrating. So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous and destruction of the enemies. We got to accept both, brothers and sisters. What we got to accept? The salvation of the righteous: we are the righteous. And you got to accept the destruction of the enemies.

You know what that's saying? Don't pray for America to stay in power. Don't pray for peace. No. Pray for the destruction of your enemies. You must accept that. That's the only way you're going to get the kingdom.

note.label: Know Your Enemy: God's Foes & Ours

points: So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. There can be no salvation without the enemy being destroyed. Salvation is the Lord coming to save you from your enemies, the same way he came down and destroyed the enemies of Israel in ancient Egypt. That is what the Passover is about: the wars of the Lord, the Lord making war on Egypt and saving his people.

Some of you are trying to save your enemy. Imagine back in Egypt, the Lord sends Moses to deliver the children of Israel, and the Israelites are fighting to save the Egyptians. That does not make sense, and it is what is happening today. The problem is many of our people do not even know who their enemy is: the enemy is the powers that enslaved and oppress you, and scripture says all the nations that touched Israel are going to answer for it.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies: you have to accept the fall of these nations as your salvation, not say Becky comes with the package.

The young men who enlist go for benefits and sign their death certificate faster, when the reward waiting is a body that cannot faint. This is a spiritual war; let the Lord fight, he is the real chess master, and enjoy the ride.
